canonical.title: Largest BST Subtree in a Binary Tree
canonical.sourceFilePath: 12. Binary Search Trees/2. Practice Problems/12. Largest BST in Binary Tree.cpp

narrative.title: Mapping the Largest Compliant Zone
narrative.scenario: A distribution yard was laid out with the sorted smaller-left rule, but some zones drifted out of compliance as stock moved. Inspectors want the biggest fully compliant zone: a subtree where every aisle still honors the ordering rule. Each supervisor reports upward three facts — zone population, its smallest and largest value — so a parent can instantly test whether merging with its children keeps the whole span compliant.
narrative.inputFormat: A binary tree as a level-order array (null marks a missing child) — not guaranteed to be a BST.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the number of nodes in the largest subtree that is a valid BST.

testCases.explanation: The subtree rooted at 5 (values 5, 1, 8) is a valid BST; the right wing's 7 spoils the root and 15.
Only individual leaves qualify — every internal node violates the ordering rule.

hintLevels: Level 1: Every leaf is trivially a BST of size one — the question is how far compliance can climb upward.
Level 2: Each node needs three facts from below: subtree size, its minimum, its maximum.
Level 3: If left.max < node < right.min, sizes merge upward; otherwise pass the best child count up and poison your own bounds so no ancestor merges with you.
